answer:
All experiments below are proposed. Do not treat a small addition of a citrate-cycle candidate intermediate as proof of a closed cycle. Run a pre-registered factorial contrast that estimates step-dependent label replacement of that intermediate by substrate carbon, and accept catalytic recycling only if that contrast, pool conservation, carbon balance, and washout or enzyme restoration converge.

## Evidence, inference, conclusion

Evidence in this package is a curator summary, not the 1937 full text or figures. It states that tissue metabolism, interconversion of candidate intermediates, and promotion of sustained oxidation by small amounts of an intermediate were combined into a cyclic model. It also states the limit that large oxidation promoted by a little intermediate does not uniquely prove a closed cycle, and it names the relevant artifacts: allosteric or bypass activation, pre-existing substrate pools, and enzyme contamination. Exact intermediate identities, isotope positions, inhibitor names, doses, and activities are unreported.

Inference: interconversion shows that steps are chemically possible; stimulation shows a kinetic effect. Neither separates regeneration from stoichiometric consumption of a pool, from respiration of endogenous fuel, or from non-cycling activation. Those alternatives make different predictions about atom origin, pool size, and dependence on a return step, so they can be separated only by contrasts that are orthogonal to “extra oxygen uptake after adding intermediate.”

Conclusion and next action: specify the candidate intermediate \(I\), substrate \(S\), and one return-step enzyme \(E_k\) before any confirmatory run; calibrate analytical limits and inhibitor or enzyme-add-back conditions in pilots; then execute the proposed design below. A positive historical-style stimulation result, if obtained, would remain ambiguous. A positive primary contrast with the validity checks would support catalytic recycling in this preparation only. Failure of any required check withholds that claim. Nothing here reanalyzes unread 1937 figures or invents those missing results.

## Concepts and what each result can mean

Catalytic recycling means \(I\) is both consumed and regenerated by a closed sequence. Net \(I\) can stay small while many molecules of \(S\) are oxidized, and carbons from \(S\) must replace carbons in \(I\).

Pool concentration means added \(I\), plus any endogenous \(I\), is net fuel. Product carbon is then limited by measured consumption of those pools. Super-stoichiometric oxidation of \(S\) is not expected.

Respiration alone means \(O_2\) use or \(CO_2\) release from endogenous fuel, independent of added \(I\) and of \(S\). Gas exchange without a carbon identity cannot establish a cycle.

Non-cycling activation means \(I\), a contaminant, or a side effect increases flux by allosteric or bypass stimulation without \(I\) acting as a recycled carrier. \(S\) may still be oxidized and the carbon balance of \(S\) may still close. Conservation of unlabelled \(I\) is therefore not, by itself, proof of recycling.

These mechanisms can coexist in a crude preparation. The design estimates them as separate contrasts rather than forcing one label onto a mixed result. Isotope exchange through reversible partial reactions can label \(I\) without net cycle flux; net \(S\) consumption and step dependence are required so that enrichment alone is not over-read.

## Primary quantitative contrast

Use a balanced factorial on independently prepared tissue units. Factors are \(S\) present or absent, \(I\) present or absent, and return step intact or blocked. A restoration arm is a separate, pre-specified reversal contrast, not an unplanned extra level. Defined reconstitution is a second stratum that must reproduce the same contrast.

Primary response is not \(O_2\) uptake. It is label-replacement turnover of \(I\) by carbon from unlabelled \(S\), with a reciprocal \(^{13}C\)-labelled \(S\) measurement of \(S\)-derived \(CO_2\).

In the reciprocal block, add isotopically labelled \(I\) and follow enrichment \(E\) and chemical pool size \([I]\). Where pool size is approximately constant,

\[
k_{\text{net}}=k_{\text{dilution}}^{(+S)}-k_{\text{dilution}}^{(\text{no }S)}
\]

\[
LRT=k_{\text{net}}\times[I]\times t^{*}/n_I
\]

\(k_{\text{dilution}}\) is the first-order decline of enrichment in \(I\). The no-added-substrate arm removes replacement by endogenous unlabelled carbon. \(n_I\) is measured moles of \(I\) actually recovered in the preparation at the first post-addition sample, not the nominal dose. \(t^{*}\) is locked after pilot calibration.

Primary estimand, intact versus blocked:

\[
\Delta LRT=LRT_{\text{intact}}-LRT_{\text{blocked}}
\]

In a balanced \(S\times I\times\) step factorial this interaction is orthogonal to the main effect of \(S\) (respiration of substrate), the main effect of \(I\) (oxidation or stimulation by \(I\) averaged over step status), and the main effect of the block. The no-\(S\) arms are the pool and blank-respiration controls; they enter \(k_{\text{net}}\) and the carbon balance, and they do not define success by themselves.

Co-recorded quantity, same units and time horizon: excess \(S\)-derived \(CO_2\) carbon per mole \(I\),

\[
\theta=\big[(C_A-C_B)-(C_C-C_D)\big]/n_I
\]

where \(A\) is \(+S+I\) intact, \(B\) is \(+S-I\) intact, \(C\) is \(+S+I\) blocked, and \(D\) is \(+S-I\) blocked. \(\theta\) is supportive only together with \(\Delta LRT\). Large \(\theta\) with \(\Delta LRT\) near zero favors activation or a path that does not regenerate \(I\).

Proposed decision rule, thresholds to be replaced by calibration limits and locked before unblinding: support recycling only if the lower 95% bound of \(\Delta LRT\) exceeds the calibrated null; chemical \([I]\) remains inside a pre-set equivalence margin while \(S\)-carbon oxidized per mole \(I\) exceeds a one-pass ceiling by more than assay error; positional enrichment matches the pre-specified one-turn map better than direct incorporation or near-site exchange; restoration returns \(LRT\) to the intact arm within a pre-set margin, while failed washout or inactive enzyme does not; and carbon recovery lies inside spike-recovery bounds. If the lower bound of \(\Delta LRT\) is compatible with zero while \(S\)-derived \(CO_2\) still rises and \(I\) enrichment and pool size stay stable, interpret non-cycling activation. If \(I\) is consumed in proportion to product carbon and replacement flux is absent, interpret pool oxidation. If gas exchange is independent of \(I\) and of the block, interpret respiration alone.

## Assumptions and unreported parameters

Assumptions, all unproven by this package: the tissue-derived preparation can be made permeable to \(I\) and \(S\) or can be studied after a permeability check; \(E_k\) is required on a pre-specified return path and can be inhibited reversibly or removed and restored; \(^{13}C\) effects are small or measured in pilot; quench stops exchange. Unreported and not to be filled from memory of the 1937 experiments: identity and purity of \(I\) and \(S\), label position, inhibitor identity and concentration, enzyme amount, cofactor concentrations, \(t^{*}\), and replicate number.

## Proposed ordered protocol

1. Preparation and quality checks. State the tissue source, homogenization or sectioning method, buffer, temperature, and protein assay. Confirm identity of \(I\) and \(S\) against authenticated standards by retention time, accurate mass, and fragment spectrum. Measure purity. Run matrix spike-recovery for \(I\), \(S\), adjacent organic acids, and \(CO_2\) trapping, including the quench. Establish limit of quantification. Assay \(E_k\) and at least four neighboring activities plus one unrelated oxidase so later inhibition is not judged by the oxidation phenotype. Screen for non-tissue respiration with a short sterile-handling pilot; if microbial activity is material, stop and change preparation rather than interpreting it as cycle flux. Record pH and cofactor stability over the intended incubation.

2. Calibration pilots, before the confirmatory allocation. Permeability: add a known amount of \(I\) and require recovery in the measured pool; if recovery fails, use a permeabilized preparation and treat that as a different system. Dose grid for \(I\), proposed only as a grid to be run, not as historical doses: about 0.2%, 1%, 5%, and 20% of \(S\) carbon. Lock a catalytic dose at which added \(I\) is recovered and is a small fraction of \(S\). Inhibitor, if used: concentration series on the enzyme panel; lock the lowest concentration that suppresses \(E_k\) by a pre-set fraction while off-target activities remain within a pre-set tolerance; then test washout by dilution, centrifugation, or dialysis until restored \(E_k\) activity and residual-inhibitor bioassay meet pre-set criteria. If washout fails, drop the washout arm and use missing-enzyme restoration only. For restoration: confirm depletion by activity assay, titrate active enzyme to the activity range of a matched complete preparation, and prepare an inactive control matched for protein and buffer. Isotope: choose positions from a written one-turn atom map that differs from direct entry and from single reversible exchange; validate fragments with positional standards; choose the shortest pulse at which enrichment exceeds a multiple of blank standard deviation without full scrambling. Set \(t^{*}\) inside the linear phase. From pilot variance of \(LRT\), calculate independent-unit sample size for a contrast large enough to exceed one-pass stoichiometry; do not invent that number here. Lock the analysis script, equivalence margins, and quench method.

3. Independent units, allocation, blinding. The independent unit is a separate tissue preparation or donor batch, not a technical aliquot. Nest technical replicates inside units. Randomize units to arms in blocks of preparation day. A person who does not assay the samples codes vials so that \(I\), vehicle, inhibitor, active enzyme, and inactive enzyme are volume-matched. Keep codes sealed until integration rules and quality-assurance exclusions are locked. Analyze \(O_2\) only as a secondary, non-decisive respiration measure.

4. Intervention and sampling. Arms, all proposed: \(S\) labelled or unlabelled crossed with \(I\) labelled or unlabelled; step intact, blocked, and restored; no-\(S\); no-\(I\); neither; vehicle; sham wash; inactive enzyme. In the defined-reconstitution stratum, wash out soluble intermediates and cofactors until target pools are below quantification, confirm depletion, then add back only cofactors titrated in pilot and, where relevant, active versus inactive \(E_k\). Start the reaction by adding the missing member of the pair after thermal equilibration. Take a mixing-time sample as true \(t_0\), then samples through \(t^{*}\). Quench by the validated method. Trap \(CO_2\) continuously or at the same times. Run the reciprocal label orientation in matched units, not as a substitute assayed only if the first result looks promising.

5. Measurements. Chemical pools of \(I\), \(S\), and a pre-listed panel of adjacent acids by the calibrated assay. Enrichment and, where standards exist, positional isotopomer fractions in \(I\) and in the adjacent acids. Labelled and total \(CO_2\). \(S\) consumed. \(E_k\) activity in parallel aliquots at start, during block, after washout, and after enzyme add-back. Protein, pH, and, secondarily, \(O_2\). Initial pools must be measured in every unit before addition. Report values below quantification as upper bounds, not as zero, when they enter the balance.

6. Controls that the contrast depends on. No-added-substrate measures endogenous replacement and endogenous respiration. No-added-\(I\) measures \(S\) oxidation without the candidate catalyst. Neither is the blank. Carbon balance: labelled \(S\) consumed, net \(I\) consumed, and measured endogenous-pool decreases must account for labelled plus unlabelled \(CO_2\) and accumulated products within limits set by spike-recovery, not by a hoped-for 100%. Defined reconstitution tests whether crude-tissue contamination or stored intermediates are required for the apparent effect. Dead-enzyme or failed-washout controls test whether restoration is specific. A bicarbonate spike checks \(CO_2\) trapping. Unlabelled matrix blanks correct natural abundance.

7. Analysis. Fit a mixed model with fixed arm effects and a random preparation-batch effect. Estimate \(\Delta LRT\) and \(\theta\) with 95% confidence intervals from the locked contrast coefficients. Do not use \(O_2\) as a covariate to “improve” the primary result if \(O_2\) is part of the respiration-alone alternative. Pre-specify sensitivity analyses for alternative pool corrections and for exclusion of units that fail quality assurance. Positional data are compared with the written one-turn map versus exchange-only and direct-entry maps. No optional stopping for efficacy unless a group-sequential boundary was written before the run.

8. Acceptance and stopping. Accept a recycling interpretation only under the conjunction in the decision rule. Do not accept it from stimulation magnitude alone. Stop before confirmatory inference if added \(I\) is not recovered, if \(E_k\) is not actually inhibited or restored, if quench recovery fails, if carbon recovery falls outside calibration bounds, or if pilot enrichment cannot detect a single turnover. A high rate of batch quality failure stops the campaign for method repair; those batches are not evidence. Early success on \(O_2\) is not a stopping rule.

9. Troubleshooting, still proposed. No label in \(I\): check permeability, quench, identity, and limit of quantification before changing the biological claim. Falling \([I]\) with stable specific activity: treat as pool consumption; do not add further inhibitors until they have passed the specificity panel. Irreversible inhibitor: switch to missing-enzyme restoration. Balance gap: test trapping efficiency and widen the analyte panel; do not assign the missing carbon to the cycle. Large no-\(S\) gas exchange: preincubate to deplete endogenous fuel, remeasure pools, or rely on the reconstituted stratum. Label in \(I\) without net \(S\) disappearance: interpret exchange, not recycling. Full scrambling at the first sample: shorten the pulse. Restoration by both active and inactive protein: suspect a non-enzyme contaminant and stop the cycle claim.

## Alternatives, limits, and what would change the recommendation

The recommendation would weaken if \(I\) cannot enter the preparation, if no step can be blocked and restored specifically, or if analytical error is larger than the gap between one-pass stoichiometry and multi-turnover flux. It would change toward activation if \(\theta\) is large while \(\Delta LRT\) and positional return remain null. It would change toward pool oxidation if product carbon matches measured net consumption of \(I\) and endogenous pools. It would change toward respiration alone if the \(I\)-dependent, \(S\)-dependent interaction is null. A hybrid of activation plus limited exchange remains possible if only some checks pass; partial passage is not a qualified success. Compartmentation, anaplerosis, and cataplerosis can move pools without a closed oxidative cycle; that is why pool size, distal-step dependence, and carbon balance are all required. This protocol cannot identify the full membership of the cycle, only whether this \(I\), in this preparation, behaves as a recycled carrier rather than as fuel, a spark for endogenous respiration, or a non-cycling activator. All numerical cut-offs above are proposed placeholders for calibration, not measurements.
